newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Half of Bangladeshi couples use birth control - UN.
newsitem.headline: Half of Bangladeshi couples use birth control - UN.

text.p: Nearly half of all Bangladeshi couples use some form of birth control, a result of government efforts to curb population growth, a United Nations official said on Wednesday.

"Fifty percent ... is a tremendous success," Alain P. Mouchiroud, a representative of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), told a news conference, marking the Dhaka release of the organisation's 1997 State of World Population report.

But he said Bangladesh should try to raise the contraceptive prevalence rate to at least 66 percent of all couples to reach a target population growth rate of 2.1 percent. Bangladesh's population is currently growing at a rate of 2.4 percent.
Mouchiroud criticised the country's maternal healthcare system. "Only 10 percent of women receive trained birth assistance in Bangladesh which is very low compared to any standard," he said.
Health officials say five women in every 1,000 die in childbirth in Bangladesh, five times higher than in neighbouring Sri Lanka and 10 times higher than in Malaysia.
